Learning FSRS helper adapter, 2026-10-23.

Upstream: https://github.com/helixnow/deep-student
Commit: 635216503c0b34bdf812e17942e0f09f51872e6f
Unmodified source: ../../upstream/src-tauri/src/fsrs_scheduler.rs
SHA-256: 62aad68b7b4a2fe1f0d43d5f2059acc35970c5a30ff6672a434be310f85c6686
Upstream root license text: ../../notices/LICENSE.AGPL-3.0
Upstream license statement: AGPL-3.0-or-later.

The helper compiles the original scheduler through a path module. It does not
depend on the separate original-check crate and does not rewrite FSRS.

New adaptation: bounded one-request UTF-8 JSON stdin/stdout protocol, typed
validation, explicit rating instead of the upstream invalid-rating fallback,
explicit IANA timezone supplied by the caller instead of process-local time,
strict memory/configuration errors instead of silent state resets, output
provenance, and passive project-owned suspension/removal eligibility checks.

The strict FSRS-6 parameter acceptance ranges are taken from the fixed fsrs
6.6.2 crate src/parameter_clipper.rs. FSRS::new uses ModelConfig::default
(one relearning step) and enable_short_term=false. Out-of-range inputs are
rejected before entering the unmodified library, instead of silently clipping
values while reporting the original inputs as effective parameters. Relevant
crate source hashes are recorded in dependency-manifest.json. FSRS itself is
BSD-3-Clause; its original notice is archived under notices/rust/fsrs-6.6.2/.

The due-time adapter is adapted from the fixed upstream
src-tauri/src/fsrs_review_service.rs::schedule_all_ratings, lines 5280-5356:
learning/relearning minutes call original learning_due_ms; review days use
now_ms + days * 86400000, preserving that upstream conversion semantics.

No Tauri, VFS, database, chat session, provider credentials, model invocation,
queue, daily limit, system clock, automatic resume, or persistence is exposed.
The project owns all scheduling records, user actions, CAS, deduplication,
pause/removal state and the unified daily review queue.

The adapter is distributed with the AGPL-3.0-or-later candidate source; actual
dependency license texts and checksums are separately archived under notices/.
Candidate checks do not establish product acceptance or final distribution
license compatibility.
